title: Private grants larger than the contributions the recipient reported
question: Are there years in which the grants these funders say they paid an organization are more than the contributions and grants the organization reported receiving?
finding: Of 1,751 organization-years where both sides are on file, 2 show grants from these funders alone larger than every contribution and grant the recipient reported in that year and the years either side: San Francisco Public Health Foundation 2021 ($2.3 million paid by 4 funders, $203,030 reported, total revenue $1.5 million); African Advocacy Network 2021 ($154,000 paid by 3 funders, $112,461 reported, total revenue $800,916). A further 27 organization-years (19 organizations, $30.6 million) fit inside total contributions only if the private grants were entered on the return's government-grants line; the largest gaps are Heluna Health 2024 ($3.6 million in private grants, $371,286 reported outside the government line); Young Community Developers Inc 2021 ($2.7 million in private grants, $42,887 reported outside the government line); Main Street Launch 2022 ($2.5 million in private grants, $0 reported outside the government line).
how: For each City-paid organization and each calendar year, the grants paid to it by the funders on file (tax periods ending that year) were set against its own Form 990 for the tax period ending that year: Part VIII line 1h, all contributions and grants, and line 1e, government grants. To allow for timing, a year is listed only if grants of $100,000 or more exceed the reported figure in that year AND in the year before AND in the year after, wherever those returns are on file. Two tests: against all contributions (first rows), then against contributions other than government grants. Matching: 17,504 grant rows were taken to be City-paid organizations, 3,430 of them on an employer number and the rest on name and address (639 of those on a one-word name, kept only with a matching address and labelled). Set aside and in no total: 969 rows ($47.1 million) where the same name is printed with an address in another city, 15 one-word names with no matching address, and $1.57 billion to universities, public bodies and organizations the City paid less than $750,000. Rows with a negative or blank amount are left out.
limits: The second test usually points at how the return was filled in, not at the money: an organization that enters every grant, public or private, on the government line misstates the split but not the total. money an organization merely holds for others, which may be kept out of its revenue; a grant to a hosted project or a same-named affiliate with its own return; money a funder calls a grant that the recipient books as a loan or a fee for service; and name matches that pick up a namesake. Funders outside this file can only make a gap larger. The record that would settle a row is the recipient's audited financial statement and its schedule of contributors. City payments set against the same returns are in the 'Do the books agree?' screens (linked in the last column) and are not repeated here.
